root.name: Modern Defense: Two Knights Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 d6 4. Nf3

overview: White develops both knights, keeping f4 or Be2 and O-O options. Black can play ...Nf6 (reaching the Pirc Classical), or keep the Modern with ...c6 and ...Nd7 (the Suttles) and ...e5 or ...b5. White aims for a solid central bind while Black waits to strike at the centre. It is a slower, quieter version of the Standard line with less attacking chances.

white_ideas.idea: Be2, O-O and Re1 or h3 and Be3, keeping a space edge
Bg5 and Qd2 for a quick attack against a delayed ...Nf6

black_ideas.idea: ...Nf6 transposing to the Pirc Classical, or ...c5 with the g7 bishop pressing

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 with both knights out against Black d6/g6, Black breaking with ...e5 or ...c5

character.notes: Quieter than the f4 lines; Black can equalise with few risks but remains cramped.

gambit.notes: No material is offered (the Tal Gambit ...Qxb2 is a rare sideline).

structure.notes: Centre not locked, resolved by ...e5 or ...c5: flexible.

approach.notes: Same Modern set-up of g6, Bg7, d6 playable against almost anything, so system.

level.notes: Few lines to learn but Black needs the right break timing.

sublines_that_differ.name: Suttles Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c6 4. Nf3 d6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black plays ...c6 with ...b5 and ...Nd7, a flexible Modern formation.

sublines_that_differ.name: Tal Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 d6 4. Nf3 c6 5. Bg5 Qb6 6. Qd2 Qxb2
sublines_that_differ.how: Black grabs the b2 pawn with the queen, a risky raid that White answers with Bxf6 and Nb5 ideas.

character.reason: Quiet positional play with space for White and counterplay for Black.

gambit.reason: No material offered in the main lines.

structure.reason: Centre in tension until a Black break.

approach.reason: Modern set-up played against nearly anything.

plans.reason: Black lets White take the centre then attacks it from the fianchetto.
